BLOCKER: AC contract contradicted: AC caps ACCEPTED at 2 per review mode, but `disposition_policy.problems` rejects every ACCEPTED, `config/review-dispositions.json` has no cap field, and docs/tests codify rejection — the shipped policy cannot satisfy the stated acceptance criterion.
MAJOR: `disposition_policy.problems` trusts a self-declared `severity` in the disposition row before the evidence-derived map (`rows.get(k).get("severity") or sev.get(...) or "MAJOR"`): a writer can label any finding "NIT" to bypass the severity gate, while genuinely unknown severities default to MAJOR and wrongly block legitimate deferrals.

`_ac_hash` (duplicated in `finalize_item.build` and `gate2_completion_check._ac_hash`) covers only `acs` + `dispositions`; test results, usage/cost and gate decisions can change after finalize without triggering `FINAL_REPORT_STALE`, and `item_revision` is never compared — merge accepts a materially stale report.

`architect_review_check` fallback accepts any diff evidence with `head_sha == HEAD` and a truthy `base_sha`, so a partial `--since` review that excluded files satisfies the gate even though part of the merge-base diff was never reviewed.

`record_gate_decision`'s new code references `item` and `backlog.get_epic(scope, project, ...)` without them appearing in the hunk — if `item` is not bound earlier in the function this is a NameError on every gate decision; the gate whitelist also still hard-refuses any gate outside {1,1.5,2,2.5}. Verify before merge.

`finalize_item.build` emits `started_at`/`finished_at` and a `usage` blob but no explicit total-time field, and its `gate_decisions` allow-list (APPROVE/APPROVE_WITH_ATTENTION/DISPOSITION_APPROVAL/REVIEW_CHURN) silently drops any other decision kind — AC requires total time and gate decisions in the report.
MINOR: `_prior_context` selects the latest review by file mtime while `_latest_review_sha` selects by the `at` field; prompt context and the diff base can therefore come from different reviews on the same item.
Persisted `final_report.item_revision` is captured before `backlog.update`, so it is permanently one revision behind the item it lives on — the field asserts a currency it can never have.
`trail.show`'s summary row renders ACs as `PASS/total` only, hiding whether the remainder are FAIL or PENDING in the top-level table.
NIT: `approval_decision`/`approval_scope` defaults are re-declared as literals in `disposition_decide.py` and `disposition_policy.py`; the config file is not the single source despite owning those keys.
`finalize_item.build` and `gate2_completion_check._ac_hash` import `hashlib`/`json` mid-function instead of at module top.
SUMMARY: Solid structural progress: disposition policy, AC gate, final-report persistence and trail rendering are wired end-to-end with tests, and prior sys.path/gate-whitelist/completion-enforcement blockers are addressed.

Top risks: the ACCEPTED policy directly contradicts the AC, disposition severity is self-declarable (integrity bypass), and final-report freshness is guarded only by a narrow hash — stale reports can merge.
Must-verify before merge: `item` binding and gate whitelist in `record_gate_decision`, and partial-diff review coverage in the `head_sha` fallback.
